core_obligations: Transport the geometric tuple: using that fibre products of affines are affine, verify that the base-changed morphisms i', pi' are again a closed immersion of finite presentation and a finite morphism with geometrically irreducible fibres of relative dimension n, that X', Z', Y' are affine, and that pi' has the required single-point fibre (proof lines 894-909).
Check the module: i'_*G' is isomorphic to F' because pushforward along the finite morphism i commutes with base change (proof lines 910-912).
Check the dimension condition: Supp(F_s) x_s s' = Supp(F'_{s'}) and the dimension of the support is preserved by base change, so dim Supp(F'_{s'}) = dim Supp(F_s) (proof lines 913-921).
proof_roadmap: Affineness: fibre products of affines are affine, so S', X', Z', Y' are affine and the base-changed tuple is geometrically admissible (proof lines 894-895).

Permanence list: closed immersions, finite presentation, finiteness, smoothness, geometric irreducibility of fibres and relative dimension n are all preserved by base change, which gives every defining property of the primed tuple (proof lines 896-909).
The two module statements: base change of a pushforward along the finite i gives i'_*G' = F', and the fibre support squares to Supp(F'_{s'}) with the same dimension (proof lines 910-921).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that an arbitrary pointed base change with affine S' turns a one step devissage (Z, Y, i, pi, G) of F/X/S over s into a one step devissage (Z', Y', i', pi', G') of F'/X'/S' over s' (statement lines 884-890). The proof is a checklist over the defining properties, and the parts that are not pure citations of a base change permanence statement are the two module-theoretic checks: that i'_*G' is exactly F', which needs pushforward along the finite i to commute with base change, and that the fibre supports satisfy Supp(F_s) x_s s' = Supp(F'_{s'}) so that the dimensions agree (proof lines 910-921). Everything reduces to those two identifications plus a list of six cited permanence results, which is why the claim is H2.
